Other scripts need a face per brand.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-dgroup"><div class="odv-dgroup-t">Brand</div><ul class="odv-tree"><li><span class="odv-dec-what"><b>Recognition.</b> The face is how each brand is known on a shared system.</span></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what"><b>Familiarity.</b> Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans and Poppins are widely seen on the web, so none feels strange.</span></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what"><b>Personality.</b> A neutral base each brand can color: the face carries the brand, the scale stays neutral.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-dgroup"><div class="odv-dgroup-t">Delivery</div><ul class="odv-tree"><li><span class="odv-dec-what"><b>Performance.</b> One family per brand: a page loads only its own brand's face.</span></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what"><b>Licensing.</b> SIL Open Font License, all three: free to embed in apps and on the web.</span></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what"><b>Fallback and pairing.</b> Each falls back to system-ui, as its tokens say; the shared scale keeps the layout steady while a face loads.</span></li></ul></div></li><li><b class="odv-lbl">Because of</b><ul class="odv-tree"><li>How many brands or products share the system? → Many</li><li>What should the brand feel like? → Neutral and adaptable</li><li>How visible is the brand in the interface? → → Touch size</li></ul></li><li><b class="odv-lbl">What it decided (16)</b><div class="odv-dgroup"><div class="odv-dgroup-t"><svg class="odv-kind-icon" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.33" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><g transform="scale(0.6667)"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></g></svg>Theme picks it sets (16)</div><ul class="odv-tree"><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.surface.highlight in light: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.surface.pressed in light: neutral.200, one step past the highlight (neutral.100), so a press reads as its own change under the finger: pressed for touch.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.action.primary.hover in light: teal.light.700: one step from the primary action (teal.light.600), so the pointer shows; its label still reads 8.34:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.action.secondary.hover in light: neutral.100: one step from the secondary action (neutral.0), so the pointer shows; its label still reads 16.3:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.action.danger.hover in light: red.light.700: one step from the danger action (red.light.600), so the pointer shows; its label still reads 8.55:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.disabled.text in light: neutral.500: 4.76:1 on surface.default, under the floor on purpose, so the control reads as unavailable. Disabled text has no contrast minimum.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.disabled.surface in light: neutral.100: the surface of a control that cannot be used, flat and quiet, so it never reads as an action.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.disabled.border in light: neutral.200: the border of a control that cannot be used, flat and quiet, so it never reads as an action.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.surface.highlight in dark: neutral.100, one step lighter than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.50), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band on the menu and on cards.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.surface.pressed in dark: neutral.200, one step past the highlight (neutral.100), so a press reads as its own change under the finger: pressed for touch.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.action.primary.hover in dark: teal.dark.700: one step from the primary action (teal.dark.600), so the pointer shows; its label still reads 13.98:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.action.danger.hover in dark: red.dark.700: one step from the danger action (red.dark.600), so the pointer shows; its label still reads 9.61:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.</span><a class="odv-go" href="foundations/color">Color →</a></li><li><span class="odv-dec-what">color.disabled.text in dark: neutral.500: 12.02:1 on surface.default, under the floor on purpose, so the control reads as unavailable. teams find their next parts ready, kept by one platform team.</p></li><li><b class="odv-lbl">Because of</b><ul class="odv-tree"><li>Who maintains the system? → A platform team</li><li>How fast does it
